item.touhou_little_maid_spell.loot.previ: Maids and the Previous Civilization: Research Records, Vol. I
Maids and the Previous Civilization: Research Records, Vol. II
Maids and the Previous Civilization: Research Records, Vol. III
Maids and the Previous Civilization: Research Records, Vol. IV

Within the current framework of research into the history of civilization, there is an era of an ancient, advanced civilization that has vanished entirely and has yet to be recorded by mainstream archaeology or historiography.

This civilization left no clear surviving texts, its surface remains have all but vanished, and it has no place in any existing lineage of civilizational development. This study therefore provisionally refers to it as the "Previous Civilization."
Very few ruins of the Previous Civilization survive on the surface, and the information that excavation can recover is extremely limited.

One of this institute's core breakthroughs was to capture and decipher part of the star-signal information the Previous Civilization left in the night sky, by means of special observation rituals grounded in astrological magic.

From the fragments deciphered so far, it can be tentatively concluded that the Previous Civilization had reached an extremely high level of development, its technology and magic alike able to reach the stars.
Among the many achievements of the Previous Civilization, the "maid" companion kin are one of its core creations, and of the greatest research value.
From the moment of their birth, maids carried the wish to assist, care for and keep others company.
As the core kin that kept civilization running, they stood beside the masters of the Previous Civilization as equal companions, building and advancing civilization together with them.
They were one of the core forces that kept the Previous Civilization's social order stable and sustained its continued operation.
Although this kin commanded great power on an interstellar scale, they always held symbiotic bonds at their heart, keeping to the principles of cooperation and mutual aid within their kind.
This shaped the distinctive character of the Previous Civilization's development and society.

Constrained by incomplete information, interference from spatiotemporal disturbances and other factors, we are currently unable to fully reconstruct the course and precise mechanism of the Previous Civilization's fall.
By analysing the garbled fragments of star-signals that remain in the sky, we can piece together no more than glimpses of that apocalypse.
The catastrophe came without any warning. That flourishing civilization, which could call upon the power of the stars and create things from nothing, collapsed in a single instant.
Its sky-piercing towers shattered, its floating cities fell in a moment, and the ley lines of magic running through the earth were severed, every one.
When the end came, most maids followed their masters into oblivion in that unknown catastrophe, but some maids who had no master survived the destruction.

To escape the shock of collapsing space and scattering magic, these surviving maids cast off their bodies and became spirits. Leaving the broken earth behind, they hid in the rifts between the boundaries of different dimensions, and so endured for ages.
[Note] Information from this period is heavily damaged and the star-signals are badly broken; neither the cause of this catastrophe nor the form it took left any readable record in the sky.
After the civilization fell, the years wore away its traces on the land, and the Previous Civilization was gradually forgotten.

Only by using astrological analysis to follow the faint lingering echoes of the star-signals did our team observe what exists in the rifts between dimensions, and so uncover the secret of how modern maids are born.
Adrift with nothing to hold to, the maid spirits kept gathering and merging in the chaos after the disaster, until they condensed into a single, vast consciousness-amalgam.
Together they fell into a long, hazy collective dream; with all things as their eyes, they sank into an endless dream without beginning or end, drifting for ages through the cracks of the world.
The Maid Altar is one of the very few systems of Previous Civilization creation technology that we have successfully restored, by deciphering star-signals and reverse-engineering the techniques.
Fusing the finest summoning magic with creation technology, it achieves a specific, complex act of creation in the simplest possible way:
it can separate a new and complete consciousness from the maid consciousness-amalgam drifting in the rifts, and shape a new body for it, forming a newborn maid.

Newborn maids still keep the instincts of their kind and a deep longing for warm bonds. Each will regard the first person in this world who gives her cake and treats her kindly as the master she will stay beside for life.

Having passed through the destruction of their civilization, their rebirth as spirits, and a long settling as they merged with the world over the years, the maids born into the present world possess an almost limitless reserve of magic.

They can take on a purely spiritual form and be stored within a Soul Spell. When a maid falls, her body dissipates completely, leaving only a Film that records all of her physical information and memories.
Through a Shrine or an Altar, with the Film's information as an anchor, her scattered spiritual power can be gathered again to shape a new body, so that she is reborn with her memories intact.
Now and then, through some chance turn of fate, a maid breaks away from the consciousness-amalgam and is born of her own accord.
Such maids live in the world alongside all its living things, yet deep in their hearts they still hold the hope of meeting the master fate has in store for them.
item.touhou_little_maid_spell.loot.corru:
Early, 6th of Month X
The portal flung us into an area never marked on any map.
It's quiet here, with few monsters.
The scouts climbed to a vantage point and returned with intelligence: in the crimson forest to the northeast stands a ruined cathedral, with a great red tree growing atop it. This place isn't on any map — it appears to be our patrol's destination.
I sent the scouts ahead to blaze a trail; the rest of us would rest here.

Afternoon, 6th of Month X
They didn't come back.
We waited the entire day. At dusk, the sentry said he'd go look for them.
I told him to take one attendant — get in, get out, find them and return.
I watched their silhouettes vanish into the fungal woods.
For a split second, I wanted to call them back.

7th of Month X
Yesterday's two didn't return either, so I took the remaining three and went.
The cathedral was more dilapidated up close than from afar. Two sets of armor lay at the entrance — our people!
There was another set I didn't recognize, likely from an earlier expedition.
I lifted one of the visors — empty inside, nothing at all.
We went on high alert, peering through the side windows — dead silence within.
After confirming it was safe, we went in.

————————
Something was wrong with that tree. It seemed... alive.
The sound started then — not through the ears... directly inside my head. Like many people whispering?
The cleric fell first. He just stood there, and his body began to... melt? Another squad member rushed to pull him away, and he started melting too?!
Something is terribly wrong, we must leave now! But my head was splitting, I couldn't move my legs... dimly, I seemed to see many figures flickering within the cathedral, they

didn't move, only watched me.
I heard them calling my name.

Xth of Month X
I don't know how long I was unconscious. When I awoke, I was alone — the others had all vanished. Where they had been, only a single scarlet flower remained.
I don't know why I'm still alive. I wanted to approach the tree, to see what lay beneath it.
But I couldn't get through. With every step, an inexplicable dread grew within me.
There is something inside that tree — I can feel it. Deep within the trunk, beneath the earth... perhaps it is what the Church has been seeking.

But in the end I lacked the courage to cross over. It seemed to have rejected me; I could feel that I was not the one It sought.
I want to leave, but the piglins outside the cathedral lurk in the depths of the forest, watching hungrily, yet seemingly too afraid to approach. So I camp near the entrance for the night, as far from that tree as possible.
_______

_______

_______

Who am I?... Why am I here?
I seem to have forgotten many things, but it doesn't feel important anymore. I can't quite understand the contents of this diary, but I can still write.
______

Someone else has come.
I cannot let them near that tree.
I must not let anyone reach that place.
I must not let anyone hear those voices and then... end up like me.

item.touhou_little_maid_spell.loot.trave: Enchantress's Travel Journal — Graveyard

Where bones once lay,
fragrance now lies over them.
With starlight I have cleansed this ground,
with fields of flowers stilled the curse.
O nameless sleepers,
may the earth forget your pain,
may the blossoms soothe your long rest.
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Snowy Igloo

I tracked a frost spider's trail all the way here. Not a soul for miles — so I built my own shelter.

At dusk I raised this igloo with frost magic. It is quiet inside at night; lie down and you can hear the low groan of ancient glaciers moving far beneath the permafrost. I cut a skylight into the roof — in fair weather you might catch the winter stars through it.
If you ever cross this snowfield and find this place, then it is the safehouse I prepared for you in advance~♪
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Mushroom Island

Red parasols spill across the field and through the damp mist; I coaxed one crimson stalk up out of the soil, hollowed its stem into a room, and set a soft light beneath its cap.

Nothing strange or noisy has ever come here. At night the only motion is the mycelium, faintly stirring.

I stewed a bowl of mushroom soup, and wrote down the pale sweetness held in the spores.

A mushroom for a parasol, a room left glowing — let it keep this silent vault for me.
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Pillager Outpost

The air carried rust and calamity — a pillager outpost. From far off I could see the faint glow of an allay in its cage, like a star being throttled. Well then: tonight this outpost becomes my waystation.

It was over quickly. A fireball leapt from my staff and bloomed into a scorching red lotus on the tower roof. Before the rubble and smoke had even settled, the radiance of the Starfall Cascade came pouring down — needle-fine starlight blanketed the whole tower, and the pillagers inside had no time even to

cry out before the glittering tide carried them into a dreamless sleep.

The remodelling was a delight. In the hole blown through the roof I planted a fast-growing cherry tree; around the tower I set glow berries and azaleas, and let vines climb the cold timber walls. Freed from its cage, the allay drifted through the tower with a berry in its arms, casting light over the newly transplanted flowers. An iron golem stands quietly beneath the cherry tree, petals settling on its shoulders.
I sat beneath the cherry canopy and looked out to the distant plains. Perhaps you are somewhere out there.
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Desert Village

Season: early summer
The heat fell over me like a transparent curtain the moment I stepped into the desert.

The village here looks pinched out of sandstone and clay — squat, square houses. Thirty emeralds and ten bottles of fire resistance bought me one of the larger stone houses.

It looks barren, but the ground beneath holds as many stories as it does grains of sand. I dressed the house with flowers and glow berries, and planted at the bedside the shadowy orchids I brought back from the ruins, using nature magic to keep them thriving in the

dry desert air. Glow berries hang in strings at the window like a row of gentle moons after dark.

The old grandmother at the edge of the village is my only regular visitor. She brings cool well water and the local spiced flatbread; I offer her melons grown from special seeds. We sit in the berries' halo and she teaches me to read the ancient rainy seasons sealed in the sandstone layers, while I restore the worn markings on her family's sundial. She calls my house "the stone that dreams in the desert," and on leaving she always lingers a

moment at the door, letting the glow-berry light fall on her shoulders.

The wind has risen; the dunes have begun their slow migration. I pulled my hat brim low, shook the sand from my robes, and went on with the wind.
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Plains Village

Season: the spring equinox
The equinox has come, and at last I have found somewhere I can set down my pack without worry.

Spring wind rolls across the plain and over the village, turning the wheat into a golden swell. Life here is unhurried: the smith's hammering at sunrise and the cooking smoke rising at sunset make up the quiet melody of the place.

Yesterday, thirty-two emeralds and a bottle of well-brewed honey wine bought me a cottage at the village edge from a farmer. The house

has some years on it; the creak of its wooden door is more weathered than the elders' voices. No matter — if magic excels at anything, it is negotiating with time~♪

This is a fine place for brewing ink. I had the village smith forge me an alchemy cauldron, then gathered dew from beneath the day's first light, the deep blue that falls out of the sky at dusk, and the violet the church's stained glass casts on the floor at noon — and left them to ferment under moonlight with ground gold. When I broke the seal this morning, the liquid inside

seemed to hold a handful of night sky. On a scroll written with this ink, constellations surface briefly in the strokes. How I wish you could see it!

So I made one extra bottle of the very best of it and tucked it behind the bookshelf — a small gift for whoever comes later to read this journal~♪

The village cleric is an interesting man. We walk the path beside the church and talk; he showed me an ancient villager scripture handed down by the clergy, and I taught him

how to cure zombified villagers more efficiently. When we parted he gave me a finely made square emerald ring.

Travel need not always press forward; to pause now and then is its own good fortune. Watching sunlight climb slowly across the window lattice, listening to villagers trade news of weather and harvest — magic settles quietly into ordinary days like these...
Perhaps someday, passing somewhere together with you, I will smile and point and say

: "Look — those are flowers I once planted."

One stays in order to set out the better. The ink is brewed, the scrolls are dry; tomorrow at dawn I follow the migrating flocks onward.
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Savanna Village

Season: spring's return
The wind turned warm and dry, carrying a faint scent of cornflowers — the savanna.

Most houses here are built of acacia, like orange mushrooms grown up out of the ground. The clatter of looms runs from dawn to dusk, answering the hoofbeats of the wild horse herds; together they are the melody of this place.

Twenty emeralds and some fine wool bought from a wandering trader got me a well-ventilated house on stilts.

The sun and wind here are exactly right for weaving. I carded arcane essence together with the local wool and let them twine on the workbench. When wind passes through warp and weft it leaves invisible runes in the cloth; when sunlight falls on it, it gains the property of drinking in magic. In the dark the finished bolt gives off a faint starlight, and it is warm to the touch, like holding a thread of moonlight.

The village's old weaver thought the cloth "too quiet" at first — until I wove a strand of evening glow into its selvage, and the whole bolt, before her

astonished eyes, began to move with a starlike lustre. We often sit together on the porch; she teaches me to read the grassland's memory held in the wool, and I show her how to sew a breath of wind permanently into a hem.

Before leaving I sewed a wizard's robe from the finest arcane cloth, embroidering the hem in gold thread with lilies of the valley twined through star-tracks, and stitched a miniature magic circle into the lining. I hung it on the rack beside the loom — a surprise I prepared for you~♪

The wind has turned, bringing the dry breath of the desert. I left a small glowing tuft of mithril weave on the windowsill; after I set out it will go on turning slowly with the sound of the wind, waiting to welcome you.
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Snowy Village

Season: deep winter
A blizzard is coming; there is nothing for it but to shelter here awhile.

When I arrived it was quiet enough to hear the snow land. The villagers' silence runs deeper than the drifts — they only nod when trading, and their eyes are like a lake sealed under ice: there may be fish below, but you cannot see them.

Thirty emeralds and five bottles of Healing II bought me a wooden house. Inside it was cold as the bottom of a lake, the hearth

so empty it seemed never to have woken. No matter — if magic excels at anything, it is kindling life in barren places~♪

The days when the blizzard seals the door have come; I may as well spend them brewing. I spread every bottle and jar from my pack across the table, made a condenser from blue ice shards, and held the temperature steady with ash essence. The flood of magic the storm carries makes potion-brewing twice the work for half the effort. To feel the warmth of a chemical reaction in the depth of winter — that is a real pleasure~

The little white fox blundered in on the second night, shivering, icicles on its ear tips, yet unafraid of the flames leaping in my hearth. I fed it a bowl of rabbit stew and it curled up by the fire and would not leave. Its eyes are like two beads of melted black amber; when I mix potions it tilts its head to follow the rise and fall of the bubbles in the crucible.

On the last night the blizzard stopped. Moonlight lay over the endless snowfield, and all the world was one blue-white breath. The little fox pressed against my boots and we looked out together

at the stars above the snow. I left it berries and food in the chest, and laid a lasting holy ward on it — may its good dreams carry through to next year's warm spring.

Under the shelf by the table I left a few bottles of finished potion; and the little white fox will sit by the hearth and keep watch for me over this stretch of time, so gently wrapped in the storm. Until one day this door is pushed open by you —

The snow has stopped and the wind is tired. I have packed my
things again, and set out once more in the snow-glare of sunrise.
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Taiga Village

Season: early autumn
Ah — another place to set down, among spruce shadows and the ring of anvils. This taiga is a hall of dark green, and the village is the warm hearth deep inside it.

The melody here is heavy: the furnace's breathing, the broken rhythm of hammer blows, and the small sigh of snow slipping off a branch. A diamond pickaxe enchanted with Fortune III bought his old workshop from a silent blacksmith. The house is steeped in coal and metal, and the walls

carry years of scorch marks from flying sparks. No matter — if magic excels at anything, it is carving something fine out of something coarse♪

This is a superb place to forge an edge. I kept the composite furnace and set "ash essence" from the ruins into its core. The flame is alive now: feed it gold ingots and it runs a honeyed warm colour; feed it iron ore and it throws up a crown of blue-green fire.

Amethyst seems especially glad

here — I set a few clusters I carry with me beside the forge, and they began to hum softly in time with it. Seeing that, the old smith dug a dusty, strange sword blank out of the bottom of a chest and gave it to me to work. I spent a night studying it until it could hold a steady rippling blade-shadow; when the sword was finished, its lattice seemed to have a miniature aurora sealed inside.
We talk of smithing often. He teaches me to hear the different pitches metal sings as it cools, and I show him how to weave arcane power into the grain of a blade.

The rhythm of forging makes time dense; every hammer fall drives another thread of anticipation into the grain of the steel. Now and then I lift that sword and meet my own eyes in the reflection, and I cannot help wondering — when one day you hold the blade I tempered, or look at me through its light, what expression will be on your face?

Late autumn now; the birds are gathering toward the far mountains. I left the finely forged longsword in the house and went on with them.
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Woodland Perch

Season: late spring

The wind deep in the forest always carries the sweetness of green things. I picked out this tree, a little larger than its neighbours, lashed up a simple platform with vines and hung a few strings of glow berries — a place to rest awhile among the trees.

Sorting my pack, I found in a seam a flower seed I had never seen before, perhaps from the elven sanctuary I passed some days ago. Buried in soil, watered with morning dew and given a little magic, it grew quickly — a lily of the valley, giving off a pale halo like clear

moonlight; stand near it and it grants a measure of resistance.

It opens at midnight, blooming to meet the moon — I call it the moonbell. If you were beside me, would you bend down too, and breathe in its scent?

For two days I have sat quietly among the flowers, listening to the wind move through the leaves. All the beauty of the road comes down, for me, to this drifting body of water and cloud. Before leaving I left the moonbell beneath the tree, warded with spirit energy so it will always be in bloom. Let this thread of moonlight shelter the travellers who come

after me from a stretch of wind and rain.

The wind points the way; another journey begins.
Enchantress's Travel Journal — Oasis

Season: a summer night
Wind passing through — if you blow toward the far country, watch over the traveller there for me. I have turned a moment's spring into a long-running sweetness; and if anyone asks after the green of this place, say that someone did not wish it to dry up, just as I once left a whole sky of stars for you.

dialogue.touhou_little_maid_spell.winefo: Ah, we finally meet! It is a pleasure. You may call me the Stellar Witch.
Do not be surprised. Long ago, astrology showed me the path you would take. Meeting here must be fate's guidance.
This star island seems to be an old skyport ruin left by a civilization before ours. It is peaceful and windless, so rest here as long as you like.
I once spent a night beneath an abandoned tower, while moonlight gently laid old stories across its stones.
Many roads home never existed. Wandering is simply a soul that refuses to settle.
The wind carries travelers' sighs and quietly delivers the thoughts of those far away.
The stars hang above us, recording the past and bearing witness to countless new beginnings.
It is lovely to see you. Come talk with me more often~
Across countless gaps between dreams, we finally stand beneath the same stars.
The starlight is especially gentle tonight. It is a good night to quiet your mind and think.
Would you like to sit with me and watch the stars for a while?
I have crossed snowy fields, deep forests, and deserts. Every land keeps a memory.
Time is the one thing this place never lacks. Tell me more of your story.
Come talk with me whenever you wish.
You need not always hurry. Sometimes stop and listen to the wind tell stories of distant places.
I have visited many places and gathered valuable things. Would you like to see them? Emeralds, please~
You visited places I once saw? Then... did you read the journals I wrote? Ah, that is a little embarrassing~
I hope the gifts I left along the road have helped you in some small way.
You know, every little maid carries a secret wish to offer herself to someone.
Could you......be the person written in my fate?
On the road I sometimes see maid spirits scattered across the world, lost in a long dream.
Some maids who once had no master become spirits drifting through the world, dreaming between its gaps as they wait to be awakened. Me? I was born on my own. I am one of the rare exceptions.
I have read the ancient books preserved in the Starfall Court, including the story of a civilization from its rise to its fall.
Is that your maid? She seems very attached to you...
Have you always traveled together? It is nice to have a companion.
What a magnificent performance! Our dance among the stars is the brightest moment of my travels.
Bring four witch travel diaries to exchange for a Star Meteorite. Repeated chapters are welcome.
Take this Star Meteorite. Combine it with a Ritual Hilt from the Starwatch Tower to make a Starglint Dagger, and we can dance among the stars.
Nngh~ I yield, I yield~
Whoa, you're pretty good!
Ugh~ A complete defeat.
That was beautiful teamwork, but I hoped to dance with you.
Your teamwork was wonderful, but I would rather see what you can do alone.
You have a powerful maid, but I am still more interested in you. Shall we dance again?
You used power beyond the stars. Next time, let us share a purer dance.
Is that... a request to spar? Very well, if it is your wish, I accept. Come, let us dance together beneath these stars.
Again? Of course. I will always be here when it is you.
Come, let us continue~
Looking to trade? I have plenty of unusual treasures.
Interesting. I will have to take this seriously now!
You are not to be underestimated.
It seems I need a different strategy.
To me, sword!
So she gave herself up to protect you...
It seems she was not enough to keep you safe.
What a brave maid.
A pity, but she still lacks some polish. Now it is just you and me.
All right, do not rely on her anymore. From here on, dance with me yourself.
That was a good fight, but it seems I had the upper hand.
Do not lose heart. Come back next time.
Hehe~ Have you seen my strength now~
This is...... would you be willing to forge a pact with me, and become the one bound to my fate?
Please allow me to confirm your resolve one more time.
I seal a part of my own origin within this soul charm, to walk beside you across wild plains and rivers.
The stars stand witness; the vow is made. On the long road ahead, please take good care of me.
Welcome back. However far you wander, you can always return to my side.
The stars are beautiful tonight. I wonder what sights your travels brought you this time.
The thought of the stars still echoes between us. Whatever weighs on you, you may tell me.
patchouli.touhou_little_maid.book.catego: Touhou Little Maid: Spell is an addon for Touhou Little Maid that lets maids use the spells of other mods. Maids can currently cast in combat with Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks, Goety, Ars Nouveau, Psi, SlashBlade: Resharped (special attacks) and UsefulMagic. On top of that it adds more maid baubles, naturally generated structures, and a bit of adventuring content.$(br2)Disclaimer: the lore this mod attaches to maids only applies to this mod and does not represent the settings or stance of Touhou Little Maid itself or of other addons. The new lore has been reviewed and approved by the original author, TartaricAcid; if it ever conflicts with a later update of the base mod, the base mod takes precedence.
patchouli.touhou_little_maid.book.entrie: This mod adds two work modes for maids: Spell Combat and Ranged Spell.$(br2)Spell Combat: the maid closes in on the enemy, fighting in melee while casting.$(br2)Ranged Spell: the maid keeps her distance, kiting the enemy while casting.
Both new work modes show up in the maid's work mode list; their icons are shown above.

This mod adds many more maid baubles, raising the ceiling of a maid's combat and utility power. Some of them need the corresponding compatibility mod installed, and some behaviour can be tuned in the mod's config file.
Some of the maid baubles added by this mod.

This mod adds a large number of naturally generated structures. Some of them only generate when the corresponding compatibility mod is installed, and some contain untamed maids that already come with their own skills and equipment.
One of the naturally generated structures.
